tasks.corrected_reference_answer: Changing the app state manager selects persistence behavior. Memory manager get/set retain live BaseState objects (reflex/istate/manager/memory.py:29-60). Disk serializes touched substates (reflex/istate/manager/disk.py:198-200); Redis also serializes touched state on set (reflex/istate/manager/redis.py:336-337). Redis retrieval deserializes bytes and recreates state on a schema mismatch (lines 229-240). Thus tests using persistent managers exercise a persistence serialization cycle that memory storage does not; this does not mean all other framework serialization disappears with memory storage.

tasks.corrected_reference_answer: Clipboard._render removes the targets prop from the Fragment and uses self.targets as its key; the comment explicitly says this ensures a different Fragment whenever targets differ (reflex/components/core/clipboard.py:57-60). Targets are separately passed to usePasteHandler in generated hook code (lines 74-92). The key controls React identity of the rendered Fragment while the hook handles listener attachment; these lines alone do not prove a parent hook must remount or that effect reruns depend solely on this key.

tasks.corrected_reference_answer: _sort_hooks partitions hooks into INTERNAL, PRE_TRIGGER and POST_TRIGGER lists and returns them in that order; missing metadata defaults to PRE_TRIGGER (reflex/compiler/templates.py:20-50). This lets templates place infrastructure before code that depends on it and user hooks around trigger setup. It is an ordering mechanism, not by itself a guarantee of all React hook rules or proof of undocumented architectural intent.

tasks.corrected_reference_answer: For BaseState.get_state, the immediate branch is the try/except around _get_state_from_cache: a ValueError falls through to _get_state_from_redis (reflex/state.py:1608-1615). The question must specify which validation error and call context before asserting a single propagation path.

tasks.corrected_reference_answer: should_use_granian honors the parsed REFLEX_USE_GRANIAN value when set; otherwise missing uvicorn or gunicorn selects Granian (reflex/utils/exec.py:296-310). Production Granian defaults GRANIAN_WORKERS through _get_backend_workers unless explicitly supplied (lines 678-679), which delegates to processes.get_num_workers; without Redis it returns one (reflex/utils/processes.py:36-46). The Uvicorn production route also uses a worker-capable server (reflex/utils/exec.py:598 onward). Process isolation and memory duplication follow worker configuration; the code does not support a blanket Granian-versus-Uvicorn strong/weak isolation or measured overhead contrast.
